I read the whole file (lines 1–298). It declares no @[simp] lemmas and no custom simp sets. Its theorems are ring identities (e.g. `(1 - σ)(1 + σ) = 0` under `σ ^ 2 = 1`) and range/ker statements with order hypotheses or `Invertible` instances. These hypotheses cannot be discharged by simp as canonical rewrites, and the identities contain no obvious normal form. Marking them simp would be the kind of annotation the rubric warns against.

Simp is used only inside proofs. `simp [← hfix, ← two_smul R]` and `simpa [sq, ← hfix, ← two_add_one_eq_three, add_smul, two_smul]` rewrite `υ y` to `y`. This orientation removes an operator application and strictly shrinks the term. I saw no credible loop or competing-rule problem there. The `simp only [... ← End.mul_apply ...]` call is a targeted, terminating rewrite. I did not run Lean, so I cannot rule out a performance issue or a simp failure.

I did not read any Mathlib simp lemmas for these shapes in detail, so I have no source evidence for a missing canonical simp lemma. I therefore report no finding.
